articles.title: SMID-Cap Outlook: The Revival Looks Set to Continue
articles.dek: The stock market is broadening as investors rotate away from the crowded mega-cap space and into the small- and mid-cap universe. What’s driving this shift?
points: Small- and mid-cap (SMID) stocks are rebounding, with the Russell 2500 Index outpacing larger-cap benchmarks like the S&P 500.
This dynamic is playing out in developed markets (DM); conversely, SMID caps have underperformed in emerging markets (EM) year to date.

J.P. Morgan Global Research expects the SMID-cap revival to continue in the short term thanks to five reasons: improving fundamentals, depressed positioning, trough technicals, geopolitical tailwinds and record valuation discounts.

articles.title: Bitcoin versus gold: why crypto is ignoring Treasury yields
Economic Impact of Iran Conflict on Oil, Gold and More
articles.dek: With $100/bbl crude, commodities markets are repricing risk in real time — with some surprising results.
points: The U.S.–Israel military operation against Iran has led to dramatic seesaws in oil markets, with Brent crude prices elevated for much of the year.

Gold’s status as a safe haven has been tested during the Iran conflict, though J.P. Morgan Global Research believes structural drivers — including central bank buying and broader de-dollarization — are still intact.

As with oil, aluminum prices could be affected by the status of the Strait of Hormuz following attacks on key Middle Eastern smelters, with an “invisible” aluminum deficit potentially working its way through the supply chain.
Overall, the conflict’s effect on global growth may prove less severe than initially feared, with J.P. Morgan economists expressing cautious optimism that a cyclical upturn could continue.

articles.title: What’s The Fed’s Next Move?
articles.dek: J.P. Morgan Global Research now sees the Fed hiking rates in December, especially as the central bank has yet to lay out a roadmap for tackling inflation.
points: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) concluded its September meeting by voting unanimously to raise rates by a quarter point, bringing the federal funds rate to 3.75–4.0%.

The hike came amid persistent inflation concerns, with core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation running above 3% every month of 2026, as well as “geopolitical developments,” according to the FOMC statement.
J.P. Morgan Global Research forecasts another quarter-point raise in December, but does not expect a longer-term hiking cycle.

articles.title: Energy Bills: Short-term relief, longer-term challenges
articles.dek: Utility bill inflation has moderated, but household payments remain elevated and longer-term pressures are building.
points: Energy bill inflation was around 4% year-over-year (YoY) in August 2026. However, Bank of America internal deposit data shows average utility bill payments rose faster, increasing 5% YoY from June through August. This was likely due, in part, to higher cooling demand during a warm summer.

But bill pressures remain highly uneven across the country. Average utility payments have risen by more than 10% YoY in cities such as Detroit, Baltimore and Washington DC, while consumers in Orlando, San Jose and Tampa have seen declines. Some of these regional differences appear to reflect policy and infrastructure factors as much as energy usage itself.

articles.title: What is the outlook for India’s stock market?
articles.dek: As global investors trim or diversify away from AI, Indian stocks are emerging as the world’s largest liquid AI hedge. Explore India’s equity market outlook and the three macro factors that will likely shape it.
points: India's equity market is starting to emerge as an “AI hedge” — a liquid, large-weight market that global investors can rotate into when they trim or diversify away from volatile AI cycles.
Earnings have been the missing engine for two years but are finally picking up, with large caps joining the recovery in mid and small caps.
Oil prices, global bond yields and El Niño are the key macroeconomic factors that will likely shape the outlook not only for the second half of 2026 but also into 2027.

articles.title: Consumer Checkpoint: Still sizzling
articles.dek: August spending remained robust as consumers sought value, income groups converged and household finances stayed healthy.
points: Consumer spending remained solid in August. Total card spending per household rose 0.9% month-over-month and 4.5% year-over-year, according to Bank of America internal data. Discretionary services continue to provide a steady foundation for this growth, despite moderation in a few categories.

Consumers still appear to be focused on value. Spending at general merchandise and big-box retailers continues to outperform more traditional retailers, as evidenced during the back-to-school season. This suggests households are actively seeking lower-cost alternatives while maintaining spending.

articles.title: De-dollarization: The End of Dollar Dominance?
articles.dek: Top dollar no more? Discover the factors threatening the dominance of the world’s reserve currency and how this is playing out across markets.
points: While the U.S.’s share of global trade has declined, the dollar’s transactional dominance is still evident in areas including FX volumes and trade invoicing.
While there are currently no scalable alternatives to the dollar, China is settling more trades in yuan, while BRICS nations are exploring a common currency to reduce their dependence on the dollar.
Currently, the dollar-centric system gives the U.S. significant geopolitical leverage beyond cheaper funding costs, including the ability to impose sanctions and control payment systems.

articles.title: The Institute Employment Report: August 2026
articles.dek: Growth in jobs and after-tax wages softened in August, but both continue to suggest a broadly resilient labor market.
points: Bank of America customer deposit account data suggests labor market momentum cooled in August, with estimated payroll growth of 1.5% year-over-year (YoY), down from 1.8% in July.

The long-standing "K" shape between higher- and lower-income households' after-tax wage growth has reversed: August saw lower-income households' after-tax wage growth of 4.7% YoY, while higher-income households' after-tax wage growth was 3.5% YoY.

Recently, there has been an increase in job switching, and the pay change associated with a job change reached the highest level in more than three years in July. This acceleration is most notable among weekly-paid employees, suggesting rising mobility among hourly and lower-income workers may be contributing to the narrowing of wage growth differences.

articles.title: Volatility is no longer the exception
articles.dek: Geopolitical shocks, commodity swings, retail flows, and rapid reversals are changing how markets move. Explore how institutional traders are managing volatility as an ongoing condition—using data, technology, and judgment to respond faster and think further ahead.
points: Volatility, now considered a defining feature of today’s markets, is forcing investors to rethink how they manage risk, build resilience, and target opportunities.
Geopolitical fragmentation, commodity disruption, and retail participation are making market moves faster, sharper, and harder to read.

Technology is helping traders process information and respond more efficiently to changing market conditions, while advances in execution tools, data, and analytics are reshaping how risk is monitored and managed.
